content: Setiap pagi tukang kayu memeriksa
perlengkapannya, sebab pekerjaan tidak
bisa berjalan jika ada satu alat yang
hilang.
= Every morning the carpenter checks
his equipment, because the work
cannot go on if one tool is missing.
Two wrappers sit one letter apart, and
Lesson 34's peeling method cannot tell
them apart by shape. Only the sense does.
per-...-an  the system, the whole set,
the standing arrangement
peN-...-an  the act, the process, the
doing of the thing
Side by side the difference comes clear.
perlengkapan  the whole kit for a job
pembuatan     the making of a thing
perizinan     the licensing system
pengembangan  the developing of it
persyaratan   the set of conditions
penghasilan   what a person earns
pertukaran    an exchange of one
thing for another
pemasaran     the taking to market
A peN-...-an noun answers to a meN- verb:
memasarkan, pemasaran. A per-...-an noun
answers to ber- or memper-: bertukar,
pertukaran.
Jika seseorang kehilangan KTP, ia harus
segera melapor ke kantor kelurahan agar
dapat mengurus kartu penggantinya.
= If someone loses their identity card
they must report it to the ward
office at once to arrange a new one.
KTP is Kartu Tanda Penduduk, the card
every adult carries. Very little happens
without it: no bank, no phone, no job.
An initialism keeps its capitals and is
said letter by letter: ka-te-pe. PNS,
Pegawai Negeri Sipil, is the other one
this pack teaches - a civil servant, and
in a village the safest work there is.
The office has a small vocabulary of its
own, and most of it came from the Dutch.
stempel   the rubber stamp; with no
mark a letter is just paper
meterai   the revenue stamp bought at
the post office and stuck on
kuitansi  the handwritten receipt that
proves you have paid
faktur    the invoice that asks you to pay
Three offices, in the order you meet them:
kelurahan  the ward: letters, addresses
kecamatan  the district: most paperwork
imigrasi   visas, and leave to stay
Wartawan televisi wajib memakai bahasa
baku, walaupun di rumah mereka sendiri
berbicara dengan bahasa daerah.
= Television reporters must use standard
Indonesian, though at home they
themselves speak a regional language.
baku means settled: the form the
dictionary prints and the state expects.
Bahasa baku is not a posher Indonesian,
it is the agreed one - of a newspaper, a
form, a classroom, a letter.
Every card in this pack is baku. That is
why a word is sometimes spelled here in a
way you will not see on a shop sign.
KBBI on the left, the street on the right.
izin       ijin                    Press 1
telepon    telpon                  Press 2
cokelat    coklat                  Press 3
salat      sholat                  Press 4
perajin    pengrajin
meterai    materai
kuitansi   kwitansi
Write the left column; read the right.
Where the street form is far commoner
(pengrajin, materai, kwitansi), the
card's note names it.
The rule reaches verbs too: KBBI turns
klik into mengeklik, and almost nobody does.
